subject: Post-call: procurement & payment routing clarification (PO vs card)
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Janet Lowe <janet.lowe@medioprov.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: procurement & payment routing clarification (PO vs card)

Janet — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the outstanding items we flagged so your AP/procurement team can confirm the commercial path: 

1) Preferred payment method: you mentioned Centro Health currently prefers PO (net 30) for third-party SaaS, but card is allowed for pilot purchases under $5k. Can you confirm that threshold and whether there is an exception path for new vendor pilots?

2) Vendor onboarding requirements: AP asked for W-9, vendor setup form, and SOC 2 summary. I'm attaching Redwood's W-9 and a short SOC2 summary for their intake. Is there an internal vendor portal or ticket you prefer we use?

3) Marketplace vs direct procurement: you said the procurement team is evaluating whether to purchase via your internal marketplace (MedioStore) or direct contract. If they choose marketplace, what are the billing/term implications (do they still require a PO from AP, or does the marketplace charge a corporate card centrally)?

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send the W-9 + vendor setup stub (attached).
- Monica (CS lead) will follow up with a short vendor intake checklist and clarify technical onboarding timelines.
- If PO is required, can you share the expected PO timing for a pilot (typical lead time)?

If helpful, we can draft a one-page mutual action plan to align commercial & technical milestones for the pilot.

Thanks — Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0122
Redwood Inference — production-grade LLM inference

Attachments: Redwood_W-9.pdf (application/pdf); SOC2-summary.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Janet Lowe <janet.lowe@medioprov.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: AP Team <ap@medioprov.com>, Procurement Ops <procurement@medioprov.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement & payment routing clarification (PO vs card)

Hi Vivek — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers from AP/procurement POV: 

- Pilot threshold: Correct — we allow corporate card for pilots under $5k, but we do require a PO for anything we intend to roll into production or for annual commitments. For a multi-month pilot where spend could exceed $5k, AP will usually ask for a short PO.

- Vendor docs: We need a completed vendor setup form (I see you attached W-9 & SOC2 — perfect start). Please also fill out our MP_vendor_setup_form.xlsx and return it to ap@medioprov.com.

- Marketplace: If the product is bought through MedioStore, billing is handled centrally by our procurement platform and typically we do not issue a vendor PO — the marketplace charges our corporate account. However, not all marketplace listings support the trial/usage reporting our teams need for a pilot.

I'll loop in AP with this thread so they can confirm whether a PO will be required for the specific pilot scope you plan. Our AP lead, Megan (ap@medioprov.com), will advise.

Janet
Director, Partnerships | MedioProv Health
janet.lowe@medioprov.com | +1 (617) 555-0910

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Vendor intake / next steps for pilot onboarding

Hi Janet — looping in on the vendor intake items and technical pilot support. Thanks for confirming the card threshold. A few items from our side to make AP intake smooth: 

- Attached is a lightly completed MP_vendor_setup_form.xlsx with our contact and tax info. Can AP confirm which fields (vendor portal ID / departmental charge code) you require so we can complete and return?

- For pilot billing options: if MedioStore supports trial usage reporting and no PO is required, we can proceed via marketplace quickly. If AP needs a PO, we typically accept net-30 PO terms for pilots and will align contract language accordingly. For the pilot itself we recommend a one-month usage window with an option to convert to an annual subscription — we can draft the commercial terms once you confirm the preferred billing route.

- Compliance evidence: attached SOC2-summary.pdf summarizing our controls. If AP needs the full report under an NDA, we can route that via our security team — let us know the contact.

Proposed next steps:
1) Janet/AP confirms whether a PO will be required for the pilot (and estimated PO issuance lead time).
2) MedioProv returns completed vendor setup form or provides a vendor portal link.
3) If PO required: Vivek and I will prepare a one-page MOU and updated price summary for procurement review.

Happy to jump on a 15-min call with your AP lead if that speeds things up — I’m available Wed/Thu morning PT.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com | +1 (212) 555-0189

Monica — thanks for the form. Megan from AP copied here — Megan, we typically require completed vendor setup + W-9. For pilots under $5k, we can usually process on the marketplace; if Redwood needs a PO please advise and we’ll run through our PO issuance cadence (usually 5–7 business days after vendor setup is approved).

Megan, I’ll leave next steps to you for vendor onboarding. If you need the SOC2 under NDA, let me know and I’ll run the NDA request.

Janet
